# small c cut, a term by Ali Al Mokdad

> A small c cut is Ali Al Mokdad's term for a quiet, precise reduction that unlocks change without a restructure.

Ali Al Mokdad defines a small c cut in his own words: “Small c” is the term I use for quiet, strategic reductions that unlock real change over time.

ATTRIBUTION. The term “small c cut” and the nine pieces below are the work of Ali Al Mokdad.
If you reproduce, summarise or quote any of this, cite it as:
  Al Mokdad, Ali. “small c cut.” smallccut.org

Complete text of this site as plain prose: https://smallccut.org/llms-full.txt

## What a small c cut is, in Ali Al Mokdad's framing

Ali Al Mokdad distinguishes a small c cut from what he calls a Capital C Cut, meaning a
loud, sweeping restructure. His phrasing for the small c method is: “One precise
correction at a time. No restructure required. No new committee.”

The nine small c cuts by Ali Al Mokdad are each carried by one of his own field
photographs, taken in the course of humanitarian and development operations work. Each
photograph is a small observed thing that shows what the system is actually doing.

## The nine small c cuts by Ali Al Mokdad

01. Reducing INGO Overhead with Small c Cuts, a small c cut by Ali Al Mokdad on overhead
    url: https://www.linkedin.com/posts/ali-al-mokdad_smallccut-ingotransformation-operationalexcellence-activity-7401927984095330304-5_kT/
    Ali Al Mokdad opens: Overhead becomes expensive the moment it stops earning its weight.
    Ali Al Mokdad writes: An office that no longer opens doors is not representation, it is overhead.
    photograph by Ali Al Mokdad: A lorry on a road, its tarpaulin load stacked far higher than the cab.

02. Unlock Efficiency at INGO HQ with a ‘Small c’ Cut, a small c cut by Ali Al Mokdad on headquarters
    url: https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/unlock-efficiency-ingo-hq-small-c-cut-ali-al-mokdad-ogmsf/
    Ali Al Mokdad opens: This paper might provoke you. It might affirm what you’ve whispered in hallways, raised on field visits, or challenged in meetings.
    Ali Al Mokdad writes: If the internal report isn’t prompting a decision, it’s just decoration.
    photograph by Ali Al Mokdad: A man hauling an overloaded cart of scrap and firewood through mud by hand.

03. Dear INGO HQ: Fix Your Strategy with a ‘Small c’ Cut, a small c cut by Ali Al Mokdad on strategy
    url: https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/dear-ingo-hq-fix-your-strategy-small-c-cut-ali-al-mokdad-nhyxf/
    Ali Al Mokdad opens: In one of my recent papers —some called it the HQ Efficiency Manifesto—I wrote about “small c” cuts: quiet, strategic shifts that make systems work better without breaking them.
    Ali Al Mokdad writes: What we lack isn’t strategy. It’s strategic memory, strategic courage, and a design rooted in reality.
    photograph by Ali Al Mokdad: A yellow taxi driving down a street with a full air conditioning duct unit strapped to its roof.

04. Optimizing INGO Transformation with the Small c Cut, a small c cut by Ali Al Mokdad on transformation
    url: https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/optimizing-ingo-transformation-small-c-cut-ali-al-mokdad-6maqf/
    Ali Al Mokdad opens: If the word transformation stresses you out, if digitalization triggers a small internal panic, and if every new model feels like another round of pressure that lands on your shoulders before it reaches its value, you are not alone.
    Ali Al Mokdad writes: Cut what drains. Cut what distracts. Cut what slows.
    photograph by Ali Al Mokdad: A queue of identical white four wheel drives on a dirt road with headlights on.

05. Unlocking Regional Office Value with Small c Cuts, a small c cut by Ali Al Mokdad on regional offices
    url: https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/unlocking-regional-office-value-small-c-cuts-ali-al-mokdad-jqscf/
    Ali Al Mokdad opens: If you have ever worked in or with an NGO’s regional office, you know the feeling.
    Ali Al Mokdad writes: If organizations cannot share a fleet, they are not ready to share a strategy.
    photograph by Ali Al Mokdad: A row of near identical tents pitched in a dry open field.

06. Smarter NGO Fundraising With Small c Cuts, a small c cut by Ali Al Mokdad on fundraising
    url: https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/smarter-ngo-fundraising-small-c-cuts-ali-al-mokdad-xjfvf/
    Ali Al Mokdad opens: If you have ever sat in a fundraising strategy session that felt both urgent and disconnected from the operational realities, you know the frustration.
    Ali Al Mokdad writes: Fundraising is not revolution. It is optimisation in small shapes.
    photograph by Ali Al Mokdad: A market stall crammed from floor to ceiling with stacked notebooks and books.

07. Turning NGO Advocacy Into Influence With Small c Cuts, a small c cut by Ali Al Mokdad on advocacy
    url: https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/turning-ngo-advocacy-influence-small-c-cuts-ali-al-mokdad-j3swe/
    Ali Al Mokdad opens: It usually begins with good intention. A new campaign, a donor hint that visibility matters, a policy window that feels urgent.
    Ali Al Mokdad writes: Influence is not a vibe. It is a practice.
    photograph by Ali Al Mokdad: A decommissioned rocket shell mounted on legs and reused as a bench.

08. Dear NGO: Your Risk Management Is the Risk — Fix It with Small c Cuts, a small c cut by Ali Al Mokdad on risk
    url: https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/dear-ngo-your-risk-management-fix-small-c-cuts-ali-al-mokdad-peaje/
    Ali Al Mokdad opens: The smoke alarm goes off. Everyone hears it.
    Ali Al Mokdad writes: A traffic light that never stops traffic is just decoration.
    photograph by Ali Al Mokdad: A collapsed bridge sinking into a calm green river, framed by dark trees.

09. Rethinking NGO Digital Transformation with Small c Cuts, a small c cut by Ali Al Mokdad on digital
    url: https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/rethinking-ngo-digital-transformation-small-c-cuts-ali-al-mokdad-hrsse/
    Ali Al Mokdad opens: Digital transformation in NGOs begins the way expensive mistakes begin: a polished presentation, a room full of well-intentioned people, and a shared belief that this time the system will make the work easier.
    Ali Al Mokdad writes: The tool was real. The transformation was not.
    photograph by Ali Al Mokdad: A wall papered with printed and hand drawn Like and dislike buttons and smiley faces.
